summary.title: Phylogenetic study of thermophilic genera Anoxybacillus, Geobacillus, Parageobacillus, and proposal of a new classification Quasigeobacillus
summary.executive_summary: This study performs a comprehensive phylogenomic analysis of 113 whole-genome sequences from the thermophilic genera Anoxybacillus, Geobacillus, and Parageobacillus. Utilizing Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI), Average Amino acid Identity (AAI), and a maximum likelihood tree of 662 core genes, the authors identify a distinct clade (I-c) within the broader Clade I that warrants reclassification. The results support the proposal of a new genus, Quasigeobacillus gen. nov., to accommodate species A. tepidamans and a specific genomospecies previously misassigned to Anoxybacillus or Geobacillus. The study highlights that analyzing these genera in isolation leads to incongruent taxonomic assignments, whereas a combined phylogenomic approach reveals clear evolutionary boundaries. While most species resolved cleanly into three sub-clades, two Anoxybacillus species (A. vitaminiphilus and A. amylolyticus) showed inconsistent positioning across different analytical methods, leaving their affinities unresolved. The research underscores the necessity of broad phylogenetic assessment when defining bacterial genera to ensure nomenclature reflects true genomic relationships.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study performs a comprehensive phylogenomic analysis of 113 whole-genome sequences from the thermophilic genera Anoxybacillus, Geobacillus, and Parageobacillus. Utilizing Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI), Average Amino acid Identity (AAI), and a maximum likelihood tree of 662 core genes, the authors identify a distinct clade (I-c) within the broader Clade I that warrants reclassification. The results support the proposal of a new genus, Quasigeobacillus gen. nov., to accommodate species A. tepidamans and a specific genomospecies previously misassigned to Anoxybacillus or Geobacillus. The study highlights that analyzing these genera in isolation leads to incongruent taxonomic assignments, whereas a combined phylogenomic approach reveals clear evolutionary boundaries. While most species resolved cleanly into three sub-clades, two Anoxybacillus species (A. vitaminiphilus and A. amylolyticus) showed inconsistent positioning across different analytical methods, leaving their affinities unresolved. The research underscores the necessity of broad phylogenetic assessment when defining bacterial genera to ensure nomenclature reflects true genomic relationships.

Research Context
DNA-DNA hybridization was the historical gold standard. 16S rRNA sequencing suffers from low resolution. ANI provides higher resolution for relatedness. AAI is recommended for distant genome comparisons. Core gene alignment offers better vertical phylogeny. The three genera belong to the family Bacillaceae. Taxonomic delimitation requires combined genomic analysis.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to resolve the phylogeny of three genera. Hypothesis: Combined analysis reveals distinct clades. Hypothesis: Clade I-c represents a new genus. Hypothesis: Isolated analysis causes incongruent taxonomy. Hypothesis: Two species remain unresolved.

Methodological Details
113 genomes were selected for phylogenomic metrics. Metrics included calculation of ANI and AAI. A maximum likelihood tree used 662 orthologous genes. Thirty-two Anoxybacillus and seventy-three Geobacillus strains. Eight Parageobacillus species were included in the analysis. One Bacillus genome served as the outgroup. Anomalous assemblies were excluded from the study. Core genes were identified using EDGAR 2.0. Orthologs were identified via BLAST against a reference. CDS were concatenated and aligned using MUSCLE. Maximum-likelihood tree was built with FastTree. ANI and AAI were calculated using ani.rb and aai.rb. Dendrograms were constructed using the DendroUPGMA web server. Unique genes were found using BLASTn alignment.

Procedures And Architectures
Geobacillus thermodenitrificans NG80-2 was the starting reference. Bacillus subtilis spizizenii TU-B-10T was the outgroup. Five assemblies were excluded for low CDS numbers. One assembly was removed as an exact duplicate. Draft genomes were concatenated with 100 N bases. UPGMA clustering used the unweighted pair group method. Trees were plotted with Interactive Tree Of Life. Six CDS were identified as unique to clade I-c. BLASTn filtering used 30% identity and 10 bitscore. CDS for alignment were from A. tepidamans PS2.

Key Results
The core gene set contained 662 orthologous genes. The tree produced 114 genomes including the outgroup. Clade I consisted of eighty-seven genomes. Clade II consisted of twenty-four Anoxybacillus genomes. ANI values separated genomes with 97.99% identity. The most distant ANI value was 95.03. The most distant AAI value was 95.81. Six CDS were found unique to clade I-c. Mean ANI suggests closer relation to Parageobacillus. GC content also suggests affinity to Parageobacillus. Two species remain unresolved due to inconsistent positioning.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Combined analysis reveals problems in delimitation. Isolated assessment fails to reveal broader issues. New genus Quasigeobacillus is proposed for clade I-c. Phylogeny must consider closely related species together. Taxonomy without broad assessment becomes incongruent. Clade I-c is outside existing genera phylogeny.

Contradictions And Limitations
Two species showed inconsistent positioning among trees. Affinities of A. vitaminiphilus remain unresolved. Affinities of A. amylolyticus remain unresolved. Merging clade I-c with Parageobacillus is an alternative. Merging would require merging Parageobacillus with Geobacillus.

Claims
Clade I-c represents a distinct evolutionary lineage requiring a new genus classification. Mean ANI suggests closer relation to Parageobacillus. GC content also suggests affinity to Parageobacillus. Trees reaffirm distinctiveness of the two species. Six CDS are unique to clade I-c. Merging clade I-c with Parageobacillus is an alternative. Merging would require merging Parageobacillus with Geobacillus. New genus Quasigeobacillus is proposed.
Broad phylogenomic assessment is essential to avoid incongruent taxonomic designations. Combined analysis reveals problems in delimitation. Isolated assessment fails to reveal broader issues.  Taxonomy without broad assessment becomes incongruent.

Data And Code Availability
Ruby scripts are publicly available in the enveomics package. Assemblies are listed in Supplementary Table S1. Removed assemblies are listed in Supplementary Table S2.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Five assemblies were excluded for low CDS numbers. One assembly was removed as an exact duplicate. Anomalous assemblies were excluded from the study.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the core gene maximum likelihood tree. Figure 2 shows the ANI UPGMA dendrogram. Figure 3 shows the AAI UPGMA dendrogram. Table 1 shows ANI and AAI values separating the new genus. Table 2 shows GC content suggesting affinity to Parageobacillus. Table 3 shows specific ANI and AAI values for genomes. Table 4 shows names and descriptions of unique CDS. Table 5 shows DNA sequences for each unique CDS. Table 6 shows BLASTn alignment results of unique CDS. Table 7 shows the best hit for unique CDS.

Three Takeaways
The study proposes a new genus Quasigeobacillus for clade I-c. Combined phylogenomic analysis is essential for accurate taxonomy. Two species remain unresolved due to inconsistent tree positioning.
